newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi suggests language or fault caused crash.
newsitem.headline: Saudi suggests language or fault caused crash.

text.p: Saudi Arabian Defence and Aviation Minister Prince Sultan suggested on Wednesday that a technical problem or language confusion between the Kazakh pilot and New Delhi's control tower may have caused Tuesday's mid-air collision between the Kazakh plane and a Saudi airliner.
"A problem of understanding the English language between the control tower and the Kazakh plane could have been the cause," Prince Sultan said.
"There may have been a technical defect but we have no confirmation," he told reporters in Riyadh.
He said the accident was an "act of fate", adding that "nobody had a hand in it" and "there was no foul play."

There were no survivors among the 312 people aboard a Saudi Arabia Airlines Boeing 747 that had just taken off from New Delhi on Tuesday evening or among the 37 people on a Kazakh Ilyushin Il-76 freighter that was preparing to land.
There was no immediate explanation for the disaster.
Speaking in the Kazakh capital Almaty, KazAir spokesman Salir Mashanlo said the Kazakh pilot lost radio contact with air traffic control in New Delhi at 1300 GMT during the aircraft's descent.

Mashanlo ruled out speculation that the aircraft's instruments or the crew's English language abilities -- the international language of aviation -- could have led to the crash. "The pilot spoke English," he said.
An Indian official said on Tuesday that the radar blips of both aircraft disappeared at 1310 GMT.
Speculation in India on the cause of the collision ranged from inadequate equipment at New Delhi airport to pilot misunderstanding of instructions from ground controllers.

Yogesh Chandra, the top civil servant at India's Civil Aviation Ministry, ruled out both. He said the transcript of the final conversations between the pilots and ground control showed both understood their instructions.
Speculation that ageing equipment at Delhi airport might be to blame was "absolutely incorrect", he told a news conference.
Prince Sultan said he was confident of the safety standard of Saudi Arabian Airlines.
Asked whether Saudi Arabia would compensate the families of the victims, he replied: "This is always the policy of King Fahd." He did not elaborate.
Indian officials on Wednesday recovered the so-called "black boxes" which could reveal what caused the crash.
